decisions.reason: This product stays close to the firm's established wooden seasonal décor capabilities, so management can readily learn from market feedback and refine it with existing craftsmanship.
As a direct extension of the firm's core Christmas pyramid know-how, it fits existing skills, materials, and customer expectations and therefore has a low likelihood of being withdrawn.

Although the electronic music box is technologically more distant from the firm's traditional knowledge base, its flagship status and the follow-on variants suggest management believes it has learned enough to continue developing it commercially.
This accessory depends on the firm's weaker absorptive capacity in electronics and licensed or themed content, and as a niche add-on it is more likely to be rationalized than retained.

As a distant, highly seasonal platform variant, it is less rooted in the firm's core knowledge and is therefore a likely candidate to be removed in favor of stronger core offerings or broader development work.
This themed Christmas pyramid builds on the firm's established design and production competences, so management is likely to keep it as a commercially understandable extension of the core range.
